comment.comment:
In 2007, a mathematician and former Wall Street trader named Nassim Nicholas Taleb wrote a famous book called The Black Swan. 

In finance and economics, a Black Swan is:

• An event that is highly improbable (rare).
• Has a massive, catastrophic impact.
• Is easily explained in hindsight (people say "we should have seen it coming"). 

Examples of Financial Black Swans:

• The 2008 Global Financial Crisis.
• The COVID-19 pandemic crashing the stock market.
• The collapse of FTX or Silicon Valley Bank. 
If you hear crypto analysts or market experts talking about a "Black Swan event," they are warning about a sudden crash or a massive, unpredictable shift in the market.
 
The Conspiracy / Pop Culture Meaning
 
In recent years, the term has been hijacked by internet conspiracy communities (like QAnon) and pop culture.

• In Conspiracy:
 "The Black Swan" is often used as a code word for a planned false-flag event, a massive power grab, or the moment the "deep state" or global elite crashes the system to reset the financial grid.

• In Pop Culture: 
The movie Black Swan (2010) starring Natalie Portman uses the concept as a metaphor for duality, perfectionism, and losing your mind.
